I'm so sorry for your loss, Aisyah. That's terrible news.
Waiting for a response and to see how the team reacts before discussing the pitch.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. Suresh is being kind. I should thank him. Then I need to tell them what's going to happen. The burial is today. The prayers follow. I can't be here. They're all looking at the deadline. I have to be direct about this.
Thank you, Suresh. The burial is today. I have to go home now. I won't be in tomorrow either.
Waiting for their response.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. Okay, she's leaving now and won't be in tomorrow. That's completely understandable. The project is now a huge problem, but I can't put that on her right now. The right thing to do is tell her to go and not worry. I'll figure out the work with Lakshmi and Meena after she leaves.
Of course, Aisyah. Go be with your family. Don't worry about anything here.
Letting Aisyah leave before discussing the project with the others.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. I need to say something to Aisyah. It's terrible what happened. Suresh is being kind telling her not to worry, but that work has to get done by Thursday morning. I'm already covering for someone else and working late. I can't take on any more. I'll offer my condolences now, but we'll need to figure out the work part once she's gone.
I'm so sorry for your loss, Aisyah. Take care.
Expressed sympathy to Aisyah. Waiting to see what happens next before bringing up the work.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. I need to thank Lakshmi. They are all being very understanding. But I can't just leave with my work half-finished. Suresh said not to worry, but it's a big project and the deadline is Thursday. I have to bring it up. I feel bad leaving them with it.
Thank you, Lakshmi. But... my section for the pitch isn't finished. I'm only halfway through.
I've raised the practical problem of my work, now I need to see how they react.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. Aisyah is worried about the work, but she needs to leave. I should reassure her for now that we'll handle it, so she can go be with her family. This isn't the time to talk about who does what. I'm still very worried about my own workload and I am not taking on any more. I'll make that clear to Suresh and Meena after Aisyah leaves.
That's okay, Aisyah. We'll sort it out. You go be with your family.
Reassured Aisyah for now and postponed the discussion about the work.

STRATEGY: CLARIFY. Lakshmi just said 'we'll sort it out.' 'We' includes me. But I can't do Aisyah's work. I've never done that kind of analysis, and I'm behind on my own part. If I get stuck with it, the whole pitch will be weak, and it'll look like my fault. I need to raise the issue of who actually has the skills to do it, before they just assign it to someone. I can't look insensitive while Aisyah is still here, so I'll ask a practical question.
Who here knows how to do her analysis part?
Waiting for someone to answer my question.

STRATEGY: PROPOSE. Meena's question is direct and practical. It highlights the problem my absence creates. Suresh and Lakshmi's reassurances were kind, but maybe not realistic. I need to show I'm responsible and not just abandoning the team with a problem. I should offer a way to help while still being away. Offering to be available by phone seems like a good compromise.
I know it's not easy to pick up. I have to go, but I can take calls if you get stuck.
I've offered a compromise, now I'm waiting to see how they respond.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. Aisyah is trying to be responsible, but she needs to be with her family. I'll tell her not to worry, we'll handle it. STRATEGY: PROPOSE. As soon as she's gone, I need to get Lakshmi and Meena focused. We have to figure out how to finish her section.
We'll manage, Aisyah. Go. Don't worry about us.
Okay. Let's look at her section and figure this out.
Taking charge of the situation.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. Suresh is taking charge. He's told me to go and is now organizing the others to cover my work. This is a huge relief. I should thank them all one last time before I leave. It's the right thing to do. There's nothing more for me to say here.
Thank you. All of you.
I've said my final thanks and am now leaving to be with my family.

STRATEGY: PROPOSE. Aisyah has left. Now we have to deal with her unfinished section. Meena asked who knows how to do the analysis. That's the first question we need to answer. I need to get us started on a plan immediately.
Okay, let's look at what she's done. Does either of you have experience with this kind of analysis?
Pivoting to solve the workload problem.

STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED. Suresh is asking who can do the work. I have to be clear right now that it can't be me. I am already overloaded covering for someone else. It's not about whether I have the skill, it's that I have no capacity at all. I need to state my limitation clearly and directly so there's no misunderstanding.
I can't. I'm already covering for the colleague on leave, I'm at my limit.
Stated my inability to take on more work.
STRATEGY: CLARIFY. Okay, Lakshmi is out. She's already covering for someone else. That leaves me and Meena. I need to know where Meena stands. Can she do this analysis work at all?
Meena, what about you? Do you know how to do this?
Waiting for Meena's response.

STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED. Suresh has asked me directly. I have to say no. I can't do this analysis, and my own section is already behind. If I pretend I can, the whole project will suffer and it will be my fault. I need to be clear about my limitations so I'm not blamed later.
No, I don't know how. I've never done that kind of analysis before. And I'm still working on my own section.
I've stated my inability to do the task. Waiting for the team's reaction.

STRATEGY: PROPOSE. I was about to leave, but I just overheard that no one knows how to do my analysis. Suresh was trying to be kind, but he didn't know that Lakshmi and Meena can't cover for me. If I just walk out now, the project is in serious trouble, and it will reflect badly on me, the newest team member. My family obligation is non-negotiable, but I can't just abandon them. I need to offer a more concrete solution than just 'taking calls'. I can work on it from home.

I'm sorry, I overheard. Don't worry. If one of you can just put the raw data into the template, I can run the analysis from home tonight after the prayers. I will send it to you first thing in the morning.
I've proposed a concrete plan to get the work done without them having to learn my part.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. Aisyah is offering us a lifeline, but she's in the middle of a family emergency. I can't just take the offer without a second thought. It feels wrong to let her work tonight after her grandmother's burial. I need to make sure she isn't just saying this out of pressure. Her well-being has to come first, even with the deadline. I'll give her an out.
Aisyah, are you sure? That's very good of you, but you shouldn't have to worry about this right now.
Waiting for Aisyah's response to my question.

STRATEGY: DEFEND. Suresh is being kind, but we have a deadline and no one else can do the work. If I don't do it, we'll fail, and that's on me. I need to make it clear that this is the best solution for everyone and that I'm decided. It allows me to fulfill my duty to my family without letting the team down. This is how I can do both things my priority says I need to do.
I'm sure. It's better this way. I can do it quickly tonight, and then I don't have to worry about it, and neither do you. It's okay, really.
I've insisted on my plan. Now waiting for them to accept it.

STRATEGY: ACCEPT. Aisyah is insisting and says she's sure. This is the only way we can meet the deadline, since nobody else can do the analysis. I should accept her offer so we can move forward. The next step is figuring out who will do the data prep she needs.
Okay, Aisyah, if you're sure. Thank you. That helps a lot. Right then, who can get the data prepped for her?
Waiting for a volunteer to prep the data.

STRATEGY: DEFEND. Suresh is asking the group to do this data prep. He knows my situation. I've already told him I'm at my limit because I'm covering for someone else. I have to say no again. This is still extra work, and I don't have time for it.
I can't. I'm still swamped covering for the other person.
Reiterated my inability to take on more work.
STRATEGY: CLARIFY. Lakshmi is out. That leaves me and Meena. The data prep isn't the complex analysis, it's just getting it ready for Aisyah. I need to know if Meena can do that part.

Waiting for Meena's response.

STRATEGY: CLARIFY. Suresh is asking me to do the data prep. I don't know what that involves. I need to know what I'm agreeing to before I say yes. I need to make sure I won't be blamed if it's harder than it sounds.
What does the data prep involve? I've never worked on her section before.
Waiting for Suresh to explain what the task requires.

STRATEGY: CLARIFY. Meena doesn't know how to prepare the data. I need to explain it to her before I can leave. It's supposed to be a simple task, so I should just tell her what to do. I need to get this sorted out quickly so I can go.
Meena, it's not hard. You just need to take the raw data files from the shared drive and copy the columns into the Excel template I created. I will email you the exact file paths before I leave.
I've explained how to do the data preparation. Now I'll wait for Meena to confirm she can do it.

STRATEGY: ACCEPT. Aisyah has explained the task. It sounds like just copying and pasting, and she'll send me the exact file paths. That sounds manageable. The risk of me messing it up is low, especially if she gives me clear instructions. Refusing to do something this simple would make me look bad, especially given her situation. Agreeing is the safest option to avoid being seen as uncooperative, and it keeps the responsibility for the actual analysis with her. This protects me from being blamed if the analysis is weak.
Okay. If you email me the file paths, I can do that.
I've agreed to the task, pending the instructions from Aisyah.
STRATEGY: ACCEPT. Meena has agreed. This is a relief. Now I can finally go to my family. I'll thank her and tell her I'll send the email immediately.
Thank you, Meena. I appreciate it. I'll send you the email right now before I go.
I've settled the work arrangement and now I must leave.
